artifacts.summary: Confirms skill_orchestrate_mint_dispatch_seq reads an ambient shell variable instead of the loop guard file; identifies Stage MT-4's existing jq read-modify-write idiom as the fix; confirms both engines share one function and one test-coverage gap.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/skills/*/SKILL.md, each fenced ```bash``` code block is a separate shell when an orchestrator issues it as its own Bash tool call — ambient shell variables set in one block (e.g. loop-guard-derived counters read at Stage 2) do NOT survive into later fenced blocks. Any per-dispatch counter minted across multiple stages must read-and-increment its persisted value from the state file INSIDE the function/block that uses it (jq -r '(.field // 0) + 1' "$file"), never rely on an ambient variable set earlier in the same SKILL.md body. skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md Stage MT-4 (line ~2086) is the canonical correct idiom to copy.
